rows.source: We compared three layouts in a small internal exercise: a table, a chart, and a paragraph summary. Each volunteer saw the same set of sample figures and answered two kinds of questions. One asked for an exact value; the other asked what had changed across the sequence. Participants found the table easiest to scan when they needed exact values, while the chart helped them notice broad changes. The paragraph summary prompted useful discussion, but several volunteers returned to the table to confirm a number. We took notes during the exercise rather than recording completion times, so we should not describe any layout as faster. The sample figures were invented for the prototype and did not represent a live service. Because the exercise used only six volunteers from our office, these observations should guide the next prototype rather than support a general claim about all readers. The next round could include people who do not work with these figures every day and could ask them to explain how they reached an answer. That would help us understand whether the apparent preference holds beyond this group.

rows.source: The cache expires entries after 30 minutes, measured from the last successful fetch. Requests made before expiry return the stored value, even if the source has changed in the meantime. The response does not start a new 30-minute period; only a successful fetch does that. Once an entry expires, the next request attempts a fresh fetch. If that fetch succeeds, the service stores the new value and starts a new expiry period. If it fails, the service returns an error rather than the expired value. This behavior matters for the settings page, where an old value could suggest that a recent change had already taken effect. The prototype does not retry the failed fetch in the background. A later request can try again, and a successful attempt will restore the normal cached path. These rules apply to the current prototype and may change after load testing. For now, documentation and support replies should describe the error plainly and avoid promising that a stale value will appear as a fallback. The cache stores one entry per requested key, so an expiry or error for one key does not by itself clear the others.

rows.source: Our tiny reading club has an unofficial rule: nobody has to finish the book to come. You can arrive having read every page, the first chapter, or just the description on the back. Last month we spent half the evening talking about a chapter none of us liked, then stayed for another hour because the conversation got good. We were supposed to choose the next book before everyone went home, but we forgot and did it in the group chat the following morning. That is fairly typical for us. We meet around a kitchen table, pass around whatever snacks people bring, and let the discussion wander when someone spots a better question than the one on our list. If you have a strong opinion, bring it. If you would rather listen for a while, that is welcome too. I would hate for a polished invitation to make the club sound more formal than it is. The only real plan is to read what we can, say what we noticed, and enjoy having other people to talk with about it. There is always room for another chair.
rows.objective: Turn this into a friendly invitation paragraph. Preserve the welcoming rule and the slightly wry, informal voice.
